## Addressing inequity in the global malaria response
The report also introduces, for the first time, a dedicated chapter emphasizing the need for a more inclusive and effective response, with a focus on reaching the populations most vulnerable to malaria. Groups at high risk of a malaria infection include children under 5, women and girls, Indigenous Peoples, migrants, people with disabilities, and people in remote areas with limited healthcare access.

## Antimalarial drug resistance challenging progress

answer: The World Malaria Report 2024 estimated 263 million malaria cases and 597,000 deaths worldwide in 2023 [1]. This was about 11 million more cases than in 2022, and nearly the same number of deaths [1]. Approximately 95% of the deaths occurred in the WHO African Region [1]. An estimated 2.2 billion cases and 12.7 million deaths have been averted since 2000 [1]. The report introduced a dedicated chapter on reaching populations most vulnerable to malaria [5]. Groups at high risk include children under five, women and girls, Indigenous Peoples, migrants, persons with disabilities, and people in remote areas with limited healthcare access [5]. The report covered malaria in 83 countries worldwide [1]. Partial resistance to artemisinin derivatives has been confirmed or suspected in at least 8 countries in Africa [4]. The 2024 edition reviews progress across prevention, diagnosis, treatment, elimination and surveillance [4]. 11 countries in the WHO African Region account for about two thirds of global cases and deaths [4].
